OpenAlex global counts, never corpus in-degree. It compares each paper's own count — not the tool's anchor figure and not the sum over its papers, which are the two tool-level numbers in Display → size by. A tool is kept if any of its papers clears the bar.

Applies at any threshold, including none. They are hidden, not scored 0 — UNKNOWN here means the paper has no OpenAlex work-id, which skews toward manuals and reports. The header always says how many are out.

A hollow node with no out-edges means we did not read its bibliography, not that it influenced nothing.

Selection

Click a node for its papers, an edge for the citations behind it.

How to read this

A missing edge is not an absent citation. Two different things produce one: we never read that bibliography, or we read it and none of its references is in this corpus — and the second is the common case. corpus in-degree measures our own harvest and is not a citation count.
